articles.title: HSBC recognised for cash management in Qatar by Euromoney
articles.description:
Doha, Qatar: HSBC has been voted by the corporate community as #1 in Qatar for Cash Management (both overall and for technology) in the Euromoney Cash Management Survey 2026, reflecting strong client recognition of the bank’s cash management proposition and digital capabilities.

HSBC was also named the #1 cash management bank globally and regionally, reinforcing its continued leadership and commitment to delivering tailored solutions that address the complex and evolving needs of clients.

Abdul Hakeem Mostafawi, CEO of HSBC Qatar, said: “This recognition reflects the confidence our clients in Qatar place in HSBC and the strength of our local teams. By combining our international network with deep knowledge of the Qatari market, we’re helping businesses respond to their evolving needs, strengthen financial resilience and pursue new opportunities. Our locally relevant cash management solutions support clients in managing liquidity, payments and collections more effectively as Qatar’s economy continues to grow and diversify.”

Nicholas Young, Head of Global Payment Solutions, HSBC Qatar, said: “Being ranked number one in Qatar for both overall cash management and technology highlights the impact of our digital capabilities and treasury expertise. Across markets, we’re focused on making cash management simpler, faster and more connected—giving clients greater control over their liquidity, improving transparency across accounts and enabling them to move funds efficiently wherever they do business.”

The Euromoney Cash Management Survey is one of the industry’s leading benchmarks, capturing the views of thousands of corporate treasury professionals worldwide.

The recognition follows HSBC Qatar’s success in the Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026, where it was named: Qatar’s Best for Securities Services, Qatar’s Best Bank for Large Corporates, and Qatar’s Best Investment Bank

Together, these four recognitions demonstrate the breadth and strength of HSBC Qatar’s capabilities, highlighting its differentiated ability to support clients across cash management, securities services, corporate banking and investment banking.

By combining global expertise with a deep understanding of Qatar’s dynamic market, HSBC continues to support businesses as they manage complexity, build resilience and capture new opportunities in an increasingly interconnected economy.

articles.title: RBI Expected to Raise Repo Rate to 5.50% in October as Inflation Pressures Build
articles.description: The Reserve Bank of India is increasingly expected to raise interest rates in October, as inflation spreads beyond a handful of categories and pressure on the rupee adds another complication for policymakers. Invest in Indian Markets and Unlock Future Potential With 5paisa! Open Account Now A Reuters poll of economists points to a 25-basis-point increase in the repo rate to 5.50% at the RBI’s October 5-7 meeting. If that happens, it would be the central bank’s first rate hike since February 2023. And October may not be the end of it. A slim majority of economists surveyed also expect another increase by December, signalling a shift in expectations after months when the RBI was largely seen keeping rates unchanged. Inflation Is Becoming Harder to Ignore The change in expectations comes as India’s inflation picture becomes less comfortable. Consumer inflation rose to 4.82% in August, moving above the RBI’s 4% medium-term target for a third consecutive month. Higher energy and food costs were major contributors to the increase. But it is the spread of price pressures across the economy that is drawing greater attention. Minutes from the RBI’s August meeting showed that several policymakers, including Governor Sanjay Malhotra, were open to raising rates if inflation became more broad-based. That condition now appears to be moving closer. Abhishek Upadhyay, co-head of economics and fixed income research at ICICI Securities Primary Dealership, said inflation for the current quarter was running about 20 basis points above the RBI’s forecast and that the increase was fairly widespread. He expects the central bank to begin raising rates in October. Nearly 60% of Economists Expect an October Hike Of the 61 economists surveyed by Reuters between September 18 and September 28, 35 nearly 60% expect the RBI to increase the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. Expectations for what happens after October have also changed. Among 53 economists who offered a view on the year-end rate, 29 expect at least one more 25-basis-point increase by December. That is a notable change from the previous month’s Reuters survey, when the median forecast suggested the RBI would leave rates untouched until March next year. Indranil Pan, chief economist at Yes Bank, said the RBI may need to recognise that it is slightly behind the curve, particularly after the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates. A Weaker Rupee Adds to the Pressure Inflation is not the RBI’s only concern. The rupee has weakened by around 6% against the US dollar this year, adding another dimension to the October decision. The RBI has spent several years managing a gradual depreciation in the currency, but higher interest rates elsewhere are making that task more challenging. Major central banks have either started raising rates or are considering doing so as higher energy prices feed into inflation. The US Federal Reserve raised rates earlier in September and is expected to deliver at least one more increase. That global shift means India’s interest-rate decision is taking place in a considerably less forgiving environment. Economists See a Relatively Shallow Rate-Hike Cycle Even if the RBI begins raising rates in October, economists are not expecting an aggressive tightening cycle. The median forecasts in the Reuters poll point to the repo rate reaching 5.75% and remaining there until at least the middle of 2028. If that view proves correct, the coming cycle would be among the shallowest RBI rate-hiking phases in at least a decade. For now, the October meeting has taken on greater significance than appeared likely only a few months ago. Inflation is running above target, price pressures are becoming more widespread, the rupee remains under strain and global interest rates are moving higher. The question facing the RBI is no longer simply whether those pressures warrant a response, but whether October is the moment to begin one.

articles.title: Bpce: BPCE and Banco Sabadell announce BPCE’s friendly acquisition of a participation in Banco Sabadell and their intention to explore strategic cooperation
articles.description: BPCE and Banco Sabadell announce BPCE’s friendly acquisition of a participation in Banco Sabadell and their intention to explore strategic cooperation Sabadell and Paris, 6 October 2026 BPCE has acquired a stake equivalent to approximately 7% of the share capital of Banco de Sabadell, S.A. ("Sabadell”) through market purchases and financial instruments. BPCE and Sabadell wish to underline the friendly nature of this equity investment, with BPCE intending to be a stable and long-term shareholder and to be represented on the board of directors of Sabadell, the fourth-largest Spanish bank, which holds leading positions in SME financing. The parties are also willing to explore strategic cooperation to make BPCE’s capabilities available to Sabadell’s clients and to create additional value together. "BPCE's investment in Sabadell is fully in line with its Vision 2030 strategic plan. It marks a further step in its ambition to develop and diversify its presence in Europe. It reflects our confidence in Sabadell’s management, strategy and long-term potential”, said Nicolas Namias, CEO of BPCE. "We share a strong belief in the importance of having deep roots in the communities and markets where we operate, serving our clients and supporting the real economy. Sabadell’s leading positions in Spain, combined with Groupe BPCE’s expertise and international capabilities, create promising opportunities for cooperation and value creation for our clients and the Spanish economy”. Banco Sabadell Chairman, Josep Oliu, stated: "We are very pleased to welcome BPCE as a shareholder of our institution. Their decision to invest in our company is a recognition of the strength of our standalone project, the work carried out by our professionals, and the growth opportunities that lie ahead. Their presence reinforces the strength and stability of our shareholder base." Marc Armengol, Chief Executive Officer of Banco Sabadell, said: "This transaction strengthens our ability to continue executing our strategic plan and generating sustainable long-term value. The investment of BPCE brings us a partner with a long-term vision and extensive experience, which we believe can complement our capabilities and help us successfully seize the opportunities presented by the market." Following this acquisition, BPCE has become a strategic shareholder for Sabadell. BPCE, the second-largest banking group in France and the fourth largest in the eurozone by shareholders’ equity, and Sabadell, the fourth-largest Spanish bank, are leading players in their respective markets. BPCE is fully supportive of Sabadell’s strategy and growth plans, as well as its management team, which has successfully led a remarkable transformation of the bank. BPCE does not intend for its shareholding in Sabadell to exceed 9.9%. With Sabadell’s support, BPCE will initiate the steps and discussions required with the Spanish and European supervisory authorities in connection with the appointment of a director to Sabadell's board, subject to applicable governance procedures and required approvals. BPCE and Sabadell intend to explore business cooperation opportunities, in particular in corporate and investment banking, equipment leasing, consumer credit, and cross-border clients business. These discussions, which the parties expect to conclude in early 2027, will aim to identify areas where cooperation could support Sabadell's development in Spain while further strengthening BPCE’s European footprint. BPCE and Sabadell will inform the market, in accordance with applicable regulations, of any material development in these discussions. About Groupe BPCE Groupe BPCE is the second-largest banking group in France and the fourth largest in the euro zone by capital. A cooperative group serving the real economy, it supports 36 million clients worldwide, backed by the commitment of its 110,000 employees. In France, Groupe BPCE relies on its major local banking networks, Banque Populaire and Caisse d’Epargne, both deeply rooted in their regions, as well as with Palatine. It operates across the full spectrum of banking and insurance activities. In Europe, it supports its clients through novobanco, the fourth-largest bank in Portugal, through BPCE Equipment Solutions, the European leader in equipment leasing, and through Oney, a major player in retail consumer finance. Internationally, the Group leverages its expertise in corporate and investment banking through Natixis CIB and in asset management through Natixis IM. Groupe BPCE draws on its diverse business lines to provide local, accessible solutions for all and to help deliver a lasting positive impact. Its financial strength is recognized by four credit rating agencies: Standard & Poor’s (A+, stable outlook), Fitch (A+, stable outlook), Moody’s (A2, stable outlook) and R&I (A+, stable outlook). About Banco Sabadell Banco Sabadell is Spain’s fourth-largest financial institution, with assets totaling €200 billion. The bank specializes in relationship banking, providing financial services to corporations, SMEs, self-employed professionals, and individual customers. With more than 140 years of history, the institution pursues a strategy focused on profitable growth, innovation, digital transformation, and supporting businesses and families in achieving their financial goals. Banco Sabadell serves seven million customers and operates a network of 1,116 branches across Spain, supported by a workforce of 13,850 employees. As of the end of the first half of 2026, the bank reported attributable net profit of €971 million, while maintaining a strong capital position and delivering attractive shareholder returns.
